Computation Beyond Death

September 29, 2026

Finally! Successful week. I feel like I've been treading water in this class thus far, but this week I finally sat down with an (LLM) tutor for an hour and cleared up everything I didn't understand.

But at the start of this week's work, I experienced a tragedy. My Arduino died. In fact, it has been dead for some time, unbeknownst to me.

In last week's labs, I overheated or shorted some circuits and the arduino was non-functional since. It took me till today to find out. Huge shoutout to Gabriel who took some time to help me understand some mistakes I made and proceed with the lab.

Here's the first board I successfully made and the associated video.

I then moved onto controlling the light with the potentiometer, which was confusing for a second because the image from the lab showed a rotary potentiometer. Still, I got it to work.

I then had some fun with buttons. This was pretty simple, but it was at this point--a few hours in--where I started to get a handle on the placement of wires and started to get an understanding of the schematic diagrams. I started to understand that I didn't need to follow the diagrams exactly if my wire was too long or short, and started to understand better the different inputs to the Arduino.

I then did the stuff with the pressure sensor! I was having fun and accidentally ripped the sensor off the breadboard.

Overall, I am just happy that I was able to actual get the wires and everything done-- I no longer feel behind. Ultimately, stripping the wires and putting them in was a big big bottleneck, especially in the beginning. So annoying! I can see why you recommended getting our own.

Looking forward to future assignments!
